statutes.title: New York Automatic Renewal Law
statutes.summary: Requires businesses making automatic renewal or continuous service offers to consumers to clearly and conspicuously present the terms, obtain affirmative consent, and provide a mechanism for cancellation. Violations are deceptive business practices.

key_provisions.description: Definitions: 'automatic renewal' means an offer that automatically renews unless the consumer takes affirmative steps to cancel.
Clear and conspicuous disclosure of the automatic renewal terms before the purchase.
Affirmative consent from the consumer to the automatic renewal terms.
Acknowledgment of the automatic renewal terms in a manner that can be retained by the consumer, including the cancellation policy.
Non-compliance: if the business fails to comply, the consumer may demand cancellation and a refund of all charges incurred after the initial term.
Violation is a deceptive business practice under GBL §349, which provides for private right of action with statutory damages of $50 per violation (minimum) and potential treble damages up to $1,000.

statutes.citation: N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law §349 (as amended by the FAIR Business Practices Act, effective Feb. 17, 2026)
statutes.title: Deceptive, Unfair, and Abusive Acts and Practices
statutes.summary: Significantly expanded by the Fostering Affordability and Integrity Through Reasonable (FAIR) Business Practices Act (signed Dec. 19, 2025, effective Feb. 17, 2026). Now prohibits three categories: (1) deceptive practices (unchanged — AG + private right of action), (2) UNFAIR practices (NEW — AG only; conduct causing substantial injury not reasonably avoidable, not outweighed by countervailing benefits), (3) ABUSIVE practices (NEW — AG only; conduct that materially interferes with ability to understand terms or takes unreasonable advantage of consumers). Violations of §527-a are automatically actionable under §349.

key_provisions.description: Deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any business, trade, or commerce are unlawful. Private right of action preserved.

Unfair acts or practices: conduct causing or likely to cause substantial injury to consumers, not reasonably avoidable by consumers, and not outweighed by countervailing benefits. AG enforcement only.

Abusive acts or practices: conduct that materially interferes with a person's ability to understand terms/conditions, or takes unreasonable advantage of lack of understanding, consumer interests, or reliance on the actor. AG enforcement only.
AG enforcement is not limited to 'consumer-oriented' conduct — can enforce regardless of whether the practice has broad consumer impact.

Private right of action: any person injured by a deceptive act may bring an action for actual damages or $50 (whichever is greater), plus reasonable attorney's fees. Court may award treble damages up to $1,000. Note: private actions remain limited to deceptive practices only.

deadline_rules.action_at_expiry: Send follow-up if cancellation not confirmed
deadline_rules.description: If the company hasn't confirmed cancellation within 7 days, send the follow-up.

penalties.description: Consumer may cancel and receive a refund for all charges after the initial term if business didn't comply with disclosure/consent requirements.
penalties.amount_or_formula: Full refund of charges after initial term
penalties.conditions: Business failed to properly disclose or obtain consent

penalties.description: Private right of action: minimum $50 per violation, potential treble damages up to $1,000, plus attorney's fees.
penalties.amount_or_formula: Actual damages or $50 minimum + up to 3x (capped at $1,000) + attorney's fees

escalation_venues.name: New York Attorney General — Consumer Complaint
escalation_venues.description: File a complaint with the NY AG about auto-renewal violations.

escalation_venues.name: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
escalation_venues.description: For NYC residents: file a complaint with DCWP.

notes: NY auto-renewal law (§527-a, effective Feb 2021) provides strong consumer protections. Key advantage: ties into GBL §349 which provides a private right of action with statutory damages, making this actionable for individual consumers. NYC DCWP is an additional enforcement venue for NYC residents.
